newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines agree to act to curb cargo fires.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines agree to act to curb cargo fires.

text.p: U.S airline executives met President Bill Clinton on Thursday and voluntarily agreed to install fire detectors in the cargo area of planes.
The agreement was announced by Vice President Al Gore, who said it represented an important step on the path toward airline safety.
"With this announcement, virtually all the airlines are saying that they're not going to wait for the regulatory process to catch up, they're moving forward on their own," Gore said.
Gore said the upgrading of some 3,700 passenger planes would begin in 1997 and cost some $400 million.
A fire in the cargo hold of a Valujet airliner is believed to have caused a crash in the Florida Everglades last May that killed 110 people.
